questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How babies' stomachs develop in the womb
What pregnant women should avoid eating and drinking at all
How to feed a newborn baby
What women eat in the first weeks after giving birth
questions.why: Beth says they're talking about what women eat and drink in the first few weeks after having a baby.

questions.q: What does Georgie say happens once a baby is born?
options: The mother gets even more care
Attention moves from the mother to the baby
The family stops worrying about food
Doctors start to focus mainly on the new father
questions.why: She says as soon as the baby is born, attention moves to the new-born baby.

questions.q: According to Allison Oman Lawi, how many extra calories might a breastfeeding mother need?
options: None at all
Fewer than during pregnancy
Up to 650 a day, more than in pregnancy
About 2,000 extra calories every single day
questions.why: She says up to 650 additional calories a day, more than she needed extra during pregnancy.

questions.q: Why did Heng Ou eat roast pig trotters after childbirth?
options: They contain collagen, which helps produce breast milk
They were the only food available
They help mothers sleep
Her doctor told her she needed to eat more fat after giving birth
questions.why: Georgie says they contain a lot of collagen, which helps produce breast milk.

questions.q: What is panjeeri, the food Ruma's mother made?
options: A spicy mix of nuts and seeds
A kind of chicken soup with spices
A sweet milk drink
A type of bread
questions.why: Beth says it's a spicy nut mix with cashews, almonds and melon seeds.

questions.q: Why was her mother's help so important to Ruma?
options: Ruma had to go back to work very quickly after the birth
Ruma couldn't cook at all
Ruma had a C-section and was on strong painkillers
Ruma's husband was away
questions.why: She had a C-section, was on very strong painkillers and was in a daze.

questions.q: How does Ruma describe her husband?
options: He left everything to her mother
He was too tired to help
He only helped with cooking
He was very involved and helpful
questions.why: She says her husband was very hands-on as well.

questions.q: What does Ruma suggest might have happened without her family's help?
options: Her baby would have been ill
She might have struggled badly and fallen apart
She would have eaten more fast food
She would have had to stay in hospital for much longer
questions.why: She says she didn't fall apart, “which I might have done if I'd been by myself”.
